display.text: Shifting every value of a random variable by the same amount. Adding a changes its mean by a but leaves its variance and standard deviation unchanged.
The probability-weighted average of net gains and losses over possible outcomes; it describes long-run average returns rather than a guaranteed return on one occasion.

The long-run average value of a random variable. For discrete X, μ_X = E(X) = Σ xP(X = x), a probability-weighted average that need not itself be a possible outcome. Also called expected value or expectation.
Rescaling every value of a random variable. For a positive constant b, its mean and standard deviation are multiplied by b, and its variance by b².
A graph of a probability distribution using bars over possible values. In the textbook's unit-width version, each bar's height and area equal the value's probability, and total area is 1.

A rule or table assigning P(X = x) to each possible value x of a discrete random variable. Probabilities are nonnegative and sum to 1. Abbreviated PMF; also called a discrete probability distribution.
A measure of the spread of a probability distribution around its mean, expressed in the variable's original units; its square is the variance.

response.correctResponse: standard deviation of a random variable

display.text: The square of the random variable's standard deviation, measuring spread in squared units. Adding a constant leaves it unchanged; multiplying by a constant b multiplies it by b².
An average that gives values differing influence. For a probability distribution, each value's weight is its probability, so more probable values contribute more to the mean.
